plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-13 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Geospatial Science program page (poid=11031) and its linked official degree map, 'Geospatial Science Degree Maps (2026-2027)', tab 'Geospatial Science (Campus)' (the workbook Index lists Online as N/A; no Online map exists), last updated/reviewed July 27, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. Per the catalog, all courses must be passed with a C (2.0) or better to be counted in the major, a minimum of 18 credit hours including the capstone project must be completed at SUU, courses may not be repeated more than two (2) times without instructor approval, and credits over 10 years old may not be accepted for use in the major. Every semester's courses sum to the map's printed semester total (15/14/15/16/15/15/15/15) and the plan to the catalog's printed Total Credits, BS Degree: 120. The catalog curriculum is exercised by the map at its 54-credit path: the Foundation Course choice (3; the map prints a generic 'GEOG/ENVS Geospatial Foundation Course' row, recorded as a choice slot carrying ENVS 1000 and GEOG 1000) plus the Core at 33, the map exercising the Statistics choice as MATH 1190 Introduction to Data Science (3) rather than MATH 1040 Statistical Inference (4), which is the catalog's 33-34 range resolved to 33 and the curriculum's 54-55 range resolved to 54. All ten fixed Core courses are placed in their map terms (GEOG 2800, GEOG 2900, GEOG 2980, GEOG 3110, GEOG 3550, GEOG 4150, GEOG 4400, GEOG 4500, GEO 4999, MATH 3410). DISCLOSED MAP-VS-CATALOG DIFFERENCES, transcribed as printed and not reconciled (Geology BS precedent): (1) the map's seven 3-credit Geospatial Science Elective rows total 21 credits against the catalog's Geospatial Science Electives block of 18; (2) the map places MATH 1050 College Algebra (4 credits, GE Quantitative Literacy) in Fall Year 1, a course the catalog's curriculum blocks do not list (the catalog program information states the program requires completion of multiple math courses and that unprepared students may need additional math preparation). The catalog's block totals (BS Degree Requirement 12 + General Education 28+ + Curriculum 54-55) do not sum to 120 on their own because a portion of the BS requirements may be met through General Education and several curriculum courses carry GE tags (the Foundation choice as GE Physical Sciences, the statistics choice as GE Quantitative Literacy, CSCY 2400 and several electives as GE areas); the map's placement, with its printed free-elective rows, is the university's own reconciliation to 120. Catalog course titles are recorded where the map shortens them (GEOG 2800 Introduction to GIS and Cartography; GEOG 3110 The Earth from Space: Intro to Remote Sensing; GEOG 4150 Advanced Geographic Information Systems Methods; GEOG 4500 Geospatial Research Project (Capstone Project)).

courses.title: Geospatial Field Methods: GPS and Drones
Geospatial Science Elective
courses.choice_note: Printed in the degree map as 'Geospatial Science Elective*'; the slot is one of the map's seven 3-credit Geospatial Science Elective rows (the four Year 4 rows are printed as 'Geospatial Science Upper-division Elective'); the catalog's Geospatial Science Electives block is Complete 18 credits from the listed Engineering Technology/Civil Drafting, Computer Science, Geoscience, Geography, Natural Resources and Humanities & Social Sciences courses, whose courses carry their own catalog credits (1-4). The variable-credit entries GEOG 2920 Workshop 1-3, GEOG 3990 Undergraduate Research in Geography/GIS 2-8, GEOG 4830 Readings and Conferences 1-4, GEOG 4890 GIS Internship 2-8, GEOG 4920 Geography Workshop 1-3 and GEOG 5570 Physical Geography Summer Workshop 0.5-5 are not carried in this slot's options because the slot is a fixed 3-credit row as printed on the map. The seven map rows total 21 credits against the catalog block's 18 (see the plan notes).
